# SEO and GEO audit: acme-mugs The repo is a small Vite + React single-page app with two routes, `/` and `/catalogue`. I read all six tracked files. Findings are ordered by severity. ## Critical **1. `public/robots.txt:1-2` blocks every crawler from the whole site.** - `User-agent: *` with `Disallow: /` stops Google, Bing and all AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others). - Nothing on the site can be indexed or cited while this is in place. - It may be a leftover from staging. If so, replace it with: ``` User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https:///sitemap.xml ``` - If you want to opt out of AI training but stay in search, add specific `Disallow` rules per AI user agent. Don't use a blanket block. **2. The site is client-side rendered only (`index.html:8-9`, `src/main.jsx:16-24`).** - The served HTML is an empty `
`. All content appears only after JavaScript runs. - Many AI crawlers don't execute JavaScript, so they see a blank page. Googlebot renders JS, but later and less reliably. - Fix: pre-render or server-render the pages. Options are SSR or SSG with a Vite plugin (such as `vite-plugin-ssr`/Vike or `vite-react-ssg`), or moving to Next.js or React Router framework mode. - At minimum, pre-render `/` and `/catalogue` at build time. The build script is plain `vite build` (`package.json:6`), so it does no pre-rendering. **3. The catalogue content is fetched at runtime (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:5-7`).** - Product names load from `/api/mugs` in `useEffect`. Without JS execution, the page is only the `

Catalogue

` heading. - Fix: fetch the data at build or server time and put it in the initial HTML. - Each product should also get its own crawlable URL, such as `/catalogue/:slug`, with a name, description, price and image. The page currently has only a flat list of names. ## High **4. `index.html:5` has the default `Vite App`.** - The title is the same on every route, because nothing updates it per page. - Give each page a unique title of about 50–60 characters, for example "Handmade Ceramic Mugs from Bristol | Acme Mugs" and "Mug Catalogue | Acme Mugs". - Set titles per route with React 19's native `` tag in each page component, or with react-helmet-async. **5. There is no meta description, canonical link or viewport tag in `index.html:3-6`.** - Add `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`. The mobile-first index depends on it. - Add a unique `<meta name="description">` per page. - Add a `<link rel="canonical">` per page. - Add `<html lang="en">` at `index.html:2`. The tag currently has no `lang` attribute. **6. There are no Open Graph or Twitter card tags (`index.html`).** - Add `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url` and `twitter:card`. These control link previews and are also read by some AI tools. **7. There is no structured data anywhere.** - Add JSON-LD in the rendered HTML: - `Organization` or `LocalBusiness` on the home page (`src/pages/Home.jsx`). - `ItemList` plus `Product` with `offers`, price and `image` for catalogue entries (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx`). - `BreadcrumbList` on inner pages. - Structured data helps product rich results and gives AI engines machine-readable facts. **8. The primary navigation isn't crawlable (`src/main.jsx:11`).** - The Catalogue link is a `<button onClick={() => navigate('/catalogue')}>`. Crawlers don't follow button click handlers, so `/catalogue` has no discoverable internal link. - It's also not keyboard- or screen-reader-friendly as a link. - Fix: `<Link to="/catalogue">Catalogue</Link>`, as on line 10. Then `useNavigate` (line 2 and line 7) is no longer needed and can be removed. ## Medium **9. The hero image has no alt text and no dimensions (`src/pages/Home.jsx:5`).** - `<img src="/hero.jpg" />` has no `alt`, `width` or `height`. - Add a descriptive alt, such as `alt="Handmade ceramic mugs in assorted glazes on a wooden table"`. - Add `width` and `height` to avoid layout shift (CLS). - If this is the LCP image, add `fetchpriority="high"` and don't lazy-load it. Serve a modern format (WebP or AVIF) with `srcset`. - The file `public/hero.jpg` isn't in the repo (`git ls-files` shows no such file). The image will 404 unless it's added. **10. The content is thin and not written for AI answers (`src/pages/Home.jsx:4-6`).** - The page is one heading and one sentence, which is too little for ranking or citation. - Add specific, quotable facts: materials (stoneware or porcelain), capacity, dishwasher and microwave safety, care instructions, lead times, shipping regions and prices, returns, and who makes the mugs. - Use a question-and-answer FAQ section, with `FAQPage` markup if it fits. - The line "Thrown by hand in Bristol" is a good entity signal. Back it with an About section and a named maker. **11. The headings are generic (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:10`).** - `<h1>Catalogue</h1>` is vague. Use a keyword-bearing heading such as "Handmade Ceramic Mugs — Full Catalogue". - Catalogue items are plain `<p>` tags (line 11). Use a list or cards, with `<h2>` or `<h3>` for the product name, plus links to product pages. **12. There is no `sitemap.xml`.** - Create one listing `/`, `/catalogue` and every product URL, and reference it from `robots.txt`. - Generate it at build time, because the product list is dynamic. **13. There is no `llms.txt`.** - Optional and not a ranking factor, but cheap to add. Put `/llms.txt` in `public/` with a short site summary and links to key pages. ## Low and housekeeping - **No 404 route (`src/main.jsx:19-22`).** - Unknown URLs return the SPA shell with HTTP 200 (a soft 404). - Add a `path="*"` route that renders a not-found page, and make the server return a real 404 status. - **There are no favicon or manifest links in `index.html`.** - **There's no analytics or Search Console setup visible.** Verify the domain in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools after the fixes. - **`/api/mugs` (`src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6`) has no error handling.** - A failed fetch leaves an empty page, and there's no loading state. - Handle both, so users and crawlers don't see an empty catalogue. ## Suggested order of work 1. Fix `robots.txt` (#1). 2. Switch the nav button to a `Link` (#8). 3. Add pre-rendering or SSR, with catalogue data in the initial HTML (#2, #3). 4. Add titles, descriptions, canonicals, `lang` and viewport (#4, #5). 5. Add JSON-LD, alt text and richer content (#7, #9, #10). 6. Add the sitemap, OG tags and `llms.txt` (#6, #12, #13). I haven't changed any files. I can implement any of these, and I'd start with #1, #8 and the head tags (#4–#6), which are small and low-risk.
